title: RWB-S9-E7016-APP: the conduct check has no operation and no named trigger, the sample of contacts and complaints has no entity or owner, the sample size and period are unpublished, "upheld" is undefined, no PRM rule row carries the conduct rules, the batch status sits with rwb-source-data and the case re-selection boundary has no published name
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.3 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S9-E7016-APP; context pack S9 rwb-partner (service row, ownership rows, Architecture v5 slides 2, 4, 5, 8 and 12); legacy RWB-E7-016; FSD S9 Partner management v3 A1.2, A1.4, A2.13 and Requirements served; TSD S9 Partner management v2 T2, T3.0 to T3.3, T4, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1, T7 and T-A; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-10, R-UNI-29, R-UNI-30, R-UNI-38, R-UNI-39, R-UNI-44, R-UNI-45 and R-LIT-22; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (partner, partner_instruction, LOV-PANEL, LOV-INSTR-STATUS, LOV-DEVIATION); Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-20 and EV-21; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-PRM-13; Business Requirements Program v4 REQ-S9-006 and REQ-S9-007
description: (1) The Ownership Map gives S9 six REST operations and none of them starts a conduct check or raises a breach: GET /partners, GET /partner/instructions, POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions, POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/accept, POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/invoices and POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results. The check is therefore carried as a conductCheck branch of InstructionWorkflow and its effect is read through the two GET operations. (2) FSD S9 A2.13.2 names the trigger as "a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer" without a name, a topic or a length, and the Ownership Map gives S9 no job, so the trigger binding is a target choice and no Schedule exists. (3) The sample is defined as "partner contacts and complaints" and no source gives it an entity, a field list or an owner: the LDM has no complaint table (LOV-DEVIATION X1 is the only complaint reference), TSD S9 T3.1 gives three partner tables with no contact or complaint column, FSD S9 A2.13 has no field catalog, and the legacy data table names only partner, decision_log_entry and rule_row. (4) The sample size, the sample stratum and the sample period are unpublished in every source. (5) R-UNI-29's condition is "a conduct or complaint breach is upheld against the partner" and no source defines the word "upheld" or who upholds it, while FSD S9 A2.13.2 step 3 only says a task is raised where a person is needed. (6) No PRM rule set exists in the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4: the conduct rows that exist are the UNIVERSAL rows R-UNI-29, R-UNI-10, R-UNI-44, R-UNI-38, R-UNI-39 and R-UNI-45 and the litigation row R-LIT-22, so no conduct rule ID can be authored here. (7) VR-S9-013-1 depends on v_ace_batch_status, an ACE view that only rwb-source-data reads, so the batch-status fact is a consumed contract that the plan's empty C row does not carry. (8) The case-side re-selection command of R-UNI-45 has no published name and no published answer shape, so the boundary is declared as Temporal with a placeholder. (9) The service is instructed to hold no v_ace_* grant (DP-05), so a direct read of the ACE batch status by this service is not available.
evidence: Context pack S9 ownership rows: six REST operations, two events (EV-20, EV-21), no job, one workflow; TSD S9 T-A.1 six endpoints; TSD S9 T3.1 seven partner fields and nine instruction fields; TSD S9 T4 "No case state machine of its own"; FSD S9 A2.13.2 and A2.13.4.4 ("None; no background event"); FSD S9 A2.13.3.1 VR-S9-013-1 and BR-S9-013; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-29, R-LIT-22 and R-UNI-45; legacy RWB-E7-016 Data, Endpoints and Test cases; Logical Data Model v8 no complaint entity
area: S9 rwb-partner (Partner): conduct check, sample boundary, rule set, trigger, batch status and case command
owner_role: Solution architect with the S9 business analyst, the rule owner in rwb-decision and the owners of rwb-comms and rwb-case
proposed: Publish the conduct rule package and its row IDs in rwb-decision; publish the sample contract of the contact and complaint owners with its field list, size and period; name the check trigger and its binding; define "upheld" and who upholds a finding; publish the case re-selection command with its answer shape; and confirm the batch-status read through rwb-source-data. Until then the story runs on the placeholders and the fakes of the contract baseline.

title: RWB-S9-E7016-CON: the sample element, the breach record element, the "upheld" outcome, the case command, the check operation and the rule set have no published baseline
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S9-E7016-CON; context pack S9 rwb-partner; legacy RWB-E7-016; FSD S9 Partner management v3 A2.13 and A2.13.3.3; TSD S9 Partner management v2 T2, T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T3.3, T4, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1, T7 and T-A.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-10, R-UNI-29, R-UNI-38, R-UNI-39, R-UNI-44, R-UNI-45 and R-LIT-22; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (partner, partner_instruction, LOV-PANEL, LOV-INSTR-STATUS); Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-20 and EV-21; Business Requirements Program v4 REQ-S9-006 and REQ-S9-007
description: (1) No source publishes an operation that starts a conduct check, so the baseline declares the two reads that answer its effect and records the check as unattended with the trigger placeholder. (2) The sample of contacts and complaints has no entity, no field list and no owner in any source, so the sample element is declared with its partner reference, its period, its scope and its set, and carries the placeholder for its fields, its size and its stratum. (3) No column of partner or partner_instruction carries a finding or a breach: TSD S9 T3.1 gives seven partner fields and nine instruction fields, so the effect stays the panel status SUSPENDED and the instruction status RECALLED and the two elements are declared unchanged. (4) The word "upheld" has no definition in the sources and R-UNI-29 does not say who upholds, so the outcome attribute is declared as the person's outcome with the placeholder. (5) The case-side re-selection command of R-UNI-45 has no published name and no published answer shape, so the commanded element carries the placeholder and the boundary is declared as Temporal. (6) No PRM rule set exists, so the record cites R-UNI-29 and the conduct rows carry the UNIVERSAL IDs and no ID is invented. (7) The sample size and period cannot be a schema default, and the service level is R-UNI-29's same-day timer read at its version.
evidence: Context pack S9 ownership rows: six operations, two events, no job, one workflow; TSD S9 T-A.1 and T-A.2; TSD S9 T3.1 and T3.2; TSD S9 T4; FSD S9 A2.13 and A2.13.3.3; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-29 and R-LIT-22; legacy RWB-E7-016 Data and Endpoints; Logical Data Model v8 no complaint entity and no finding column
area: S9 rwb-partner (Partner): contract baseline of the conduct-check path
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-partner tech lead, the rule owner in rwb-decision and the owners of the sample and the case command
proposed: Publish the sample contract and its owner, the definition of "upheld" and the outcome the person records, the case re-selection command with its answer shape, and the conduct rule package in rwb-decision. The baseline is then re-tagged without a new major version where the change is additive, and with one where an attribute is renamed.
